Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — Sunday is a windy day ahead of an approaching storm, and most sites are unflyable. Strong southwest flow over the Sierra crest builds to 41–45 knots from noon to 2pm and puts the high launches in strong, turbulent lee-side wind. Thermals are weak at most launches, and cloud lowers onto the higher terrain from midday. McClellan offers the only realistic window, and it is marginal: roughly 11am–2pm, for experienced pilots comfortable in strong wind.

Site Breakdown

No site rated favorable today.

Not recommended today (9) — click a row for details

McClellan Marginal — Launch wind is aligned and flyable from late morning, but thermals are weak and strong flow above means turbulence.
Window: 11am–2pm
In the window, thermals peak at 156 ft/min at noon and the thermal top is 1,181–1,735 ft AGL. Launch wind is 8–18 mph from 200–234°, which is on the launch. Ridge lift is good at noon and 1pm, at +475 and +393 ft/min. Above launch the wind gets much stronger: 23–29 mph at 1,000 ft and 41–46 mph at 3,000 ft above ground. Low-level wind shear, meaning a sharp change in wind over a short height, reaches 9 mph per 100 m near 1,871 ft AGL, which is caution level. Do not climb far above the ridge, and land early as the crest flow peaks.
Daydreams Marginal — Launch-aligned wind lasts only about an hour, with hazardous wind shear and wind building to 25 mph by noon.
Window: 11am–noon
At 11am, launch wind is 17 mph from 241°, thermals are 133 ft/min with a thermal top near 1,000 ft AGL, and ridge lift is +412 ft/min. By noon, wind reaches 25 mph with a 26 mph peak 10 m wind. Wind shear peaks at 10 mph per 100 m with a 33° turn near 738 ft AGL, which is hazardous. At 3pm the wind is 12 mph from 237° again, but cloud base is only about 700 ft above launch. The model also shows a trace of rain at 1pm. Advanced pilots only.
Kingsbury grade Unfavorable — The wind never lines up with the southeast launch and blows across or behind it all day, with very strong wind just above.
Thermal strength (w*) peaks at 234 ft/min around 11am, with the thermal top (height of the mixed layer) near 1,900 ft above ground level (AGL). Launch wind is light and variable early, then comes from 193–244° and climbs to 26 mph by 1pm. Wind at 3,000 ft above ground is 42–61 mph through the day. None of the hours fall in the preferred 74–134° range.
Hallelujah Unfavorable — Morning wind is too strong, and from noon on it swings south to southeast, off the west/southwest launch.
Launch wind is 27–33 mph from about 190° from 8 to 11am, with 43 mph at 1,000 ft above ground. Midday it eases to 15–18 mph but turns to 151–182°, outside the preferred 225–315°. Thermals peak at 300 ft/min at noon, with the thermal top near 2,300 ft AGL. Cloud cover reaches 89–100% from 1pm, with base about 2,600–2,800 ft above launch.
Slide Mountain Unfavorable — The launch is in strong lee-side sink all day, there are no thermals, and cloud base drops to launch level from noon.
Launch wind is 30–38 mph from 226–242°, which puts the south/southeast launch downwind. Ridge lift is strongly negative at -930 to -1,244 ft/min, meaning sinking air. Wind at 1,000 ft above ground is 56–69 mph. Thermal strength is 0 ft/min all day. Cloud base, or the height where rising air forms cloud, is 0–97 ft above launch from noon, and the site is flagged for rain. With launch temperatures of 34–37 °F, expect a wet or possibly iced wing.
West McClellan Unfavorable — The wind stays south of the west launch and reaches 21–27 mph midday, with almost no thermals.
Launch wind is 186–223° all day, outside the preferred 240–300°. It builds from 11 mph at 8am to 27 mph with a peak 10 m wind of 30 mph at noon. Thermal strength is at most 59 ft/min. Wind at 3,000 ft above ground is about 46–54 mph.
Peavine Mountain Unfavorable — The launch has 27–43 mph wind all day, lee-side sink, and cloud down to launch level from 1pm.
Launch wind is 40–43 mph from about 211–220° in the morning and never drops below 27 mph. Ridge lift is negative all day, at -130 to -227 ft/min. Wind at 1,000 ft above ground is 38–63 mph. Thermals peak at only 172 ft/min. Cloud covers 89–100% from noon with base 0–600 ft above launch. The launch is 35–36 °F, and the freezing level dips to 700 ft above launch.
Rainbow Ridge Unfavorable — The wind comes from the south to west all day, never from the east/northeast that this launch needs.
Launch wind is 3–11 mph from 136–285°, outside the preferred 22–112°. Thermals are at most 49 ft/min. Cloud covers 89–100% from 10am to 3pm. Low-level wind shear of 12 mph per 100 m near 2,327 ft AGL is in the hazardous range.
Duck Hill Unfavorable — The wind blows from the south-southeast, behind the west-to-north launch, all day and into the evening.
Launch wind is 5–17 mph from 116–197°, outside the preferred 270–50°. The 4pm reading is 5 mph from 197°, so there is no evening soaring either. Thermal strength is 0 ft/min. The air cools quickly with height (8.3 °C per km, which favors sharp, punchy thermals), but the model shows no usable thermals here.

Hazards

  • Lee-side turbulence and mountain wave: Southwest wind at Sierra crest height is 36 knots at 8am, 45 knots at noon, and 41–42 knots from 1–2pm, all from 219–235°. That is strong enough for rotor, wave turbulence and gusty downslope wind east of the Carson Range and downwind of Peavine. NWS Reno forecasts Sierra ridge gusts of 70–80 mph Sunday morning, rising above 95 mph, and mentions mountain wave turbulence.
  • Strong wind at high launches: Peavine is forecast at 27–43 mph and Slide Mountain at 30–38 mph all day, with 56–69 mph at 1,000 ft above both. NWS Reno has a Lake Wind Advisory from 7 AM Sunday and expects Nevada valley gusts of 30–40 mph.
  • Low-level wind shear: Shear reaches hazardous levels at Rainbow Ridge (12 mph per 100 m) and Daydreams (10 mph per 100 m), and caution levels of 9 mph per 100 m at McClellan, West McClellan, Kingsbury and Duck Hill. NWS Reno also expects periods of low-level wind shear (LLWS) Sunday morning.
  • Cloud on high terrain and icing: From noon, cloud base drops to launch level at Slide Mountain and Peavine. Peavine launch is 35–36 °F and Slide 34–37 °F, with the freezing level only 700–1,100 ft above those launches. Expect poor visibility and a risk of iced or wet gear.
  • Incoming rain: The model shows rain at Slide Mountain and only a trace (0.1 mm) at Daydreams at 1pm. NWS Reno expects precipitation in the Sierra from midday Sunday with light spillover onto the Sierra Front (50–70% chance), plus a 15% chance of lightning in the Sierra Sunday afternoon.
  • Forecast confidence: In the first hours of this run, modeled wind at the Slide Mountain summit station ran far above observed, 50–58 mph versus 13–26 mph, so winds aloft may be overstated. Those early hours are weak evidence, and NWS Reno also expects very strong ridge winds, so treat the strong-wind picture as likely.
